entries.name: CI_CLEANUP_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S
entries.notes: The --timeout option takes priority over the variable. When --timeout is not given, a value that does not match the format, or that is zero, makes the script exit with an argparse error (status 2). The empty text is also rejected. When --timeout is given, the variable is not checked at all: argparse converts a text default only for an option that is absent from the command line. bin/slice imports remove_fuse_root from this file (bin/slice:55) and does not use the variable. No file in this area sets it. Count for the checker: the literal name is on 1 lines of the 63 files of this area (0 of them in the two test directories).

readers.mechanism: os.environ.get as the argparse default of --timeout

entries.values: A positive number with an optional unit letter: s (seconds), m (minutes), h (hours) or d (days). No letter means seconds. Examples: 10s, 0.1s, 2m.

entries.default: Unset: 10s (10 seconds). An empty value is not treated as unset. It fails the duration check. A --timeout argument to the wrapper replaces the variable.
entries.effect: Time limit for each external command of the FUSE cleanup: each unmount command (fusermount -uz) and the final 'rm -rf --one-file-system'. When a command runs longer, the program sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL to its process group and the cleanup fails.

entries.notes: ci-cleanup-fuse-mount.sh does not name the variable. doc_mentions.claim: The Dice daemon sets it before launching the dispatched subprocess, for example DICE_SLOTS=0,1,2,3. The value is a comma-separated list of absolute slot ids.
Shared-mode children always receive their active slot grant as DICE_SLOTS.
The inner pass of "bin/slice run" reads slot grants in this order: internal --slot-mask flag, daemon-marked $DICE_SLOTS, $SYSTEM_CONFIG.
Only the inner "bin/slice run" and "bin/slice bench" path may consume a contiguous DICE_SLOTS grant that --instance cannot represent.
A daemon-marked DICE_SLOTS value gives the Slice packer its slot universe.

entries.default: Unset or empty: not read unless DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is 1. With DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1 an unset or empty value fails startup with 'Incomplete Dice grant environment'.
entries.effect: Names the slots that the Dice daemon granted to this process. A slot is one equal share of the server (FPGA cards, CPU cores, memory). The built-in layout has 4 slots per NUMA node, and the code counts one NUMA node per CPU package (src/system/system.cpp:1167-1194, 300-307). The C++ code works out the one --instance that these slots form and takes the permitted cards, cores and NUMA nodes from them.
entries.name: DICE_SLOTS
entries.notes: Read only when DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is 1. Rules (src/system/system.cpp:1689-1708): the slots must be one unbroken run, the run length must divide the total slot count, the first slot must be a multiple of the run length, and the last slot must be below the total. The --instance in SYSTEM_CONFIG must describe the same slots, or startup fails with 'SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance does not match DICE_SLOTS' or a 'Dice grant' conflict message. Python tools also read the name (bin/rinzler:472, bin/runtron:491). Those files belong to another sweep.

rederive.audience_reason: Read by deployed rinzler and runtron in grant mode. It decides which cards, cores and memory nodes the process may use. The Dice daemon sets it.
rederive.default: Not read unless DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is exactly 1. The two C++ functions that read it (dice_grant_env_complete and the functions below) are reached only in grant mode. In grant mode an unset value fails startup with 'Incomplete Dice grant environment; launch through Dice again' (src/system/system.cpp:1667).
rederive.effect: Names the slots that the Dice daemon granted to this process. A slot is one equal share of the server (FPGA cards, CPU cores, memory). The C++ code works out the one --instance that the slots form: instance id = first slot / run length, instance count = total slots / run length (src/system/system.cpp:1697-1698). It takes the permitted cards, CPU cores and NUMA nodes for these slots from the trusted resource map, or from the built-in table when no map matches (src/system/system.cpp:1699-1708).
rederive.empty_value: Same as unset. In grant mode startup fails with the 'Incomplete Dice grant environment' message.
rederive.how_to_check: On success the instance worked out from the slots shows in 'Configured instance <id>,<count> using resource map (<path>).' (src/system/system.cpp:1986) or 'Configured instance <id>,<count> using hardcoded settings.' (src/system/system.cpp:1989). These lines also appear without Dice. The slot list itself is printed only in the error lines listed under invalid_value.
rederive.interactions: Read only in grant mode (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1). The --instance in SYSTEM_CONFIG must describe the same slots. If not, startup fails with 'Dice grant <id>: --instance requested '<x,y>'; permitted --instance <a>,<b> (slots [...])' (src/system/system.cpp:1789-1795) or 'SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance does not match DICE_SLOTS' (src/system/system.cpp:1512). The Python tools parse the same variable with looser rules. bin/slice accepts ranges such as 0-7 and spaces (parse_slot_mask, bin/slice:1115-1138). bin/rinzler accepts spaces and empty items (bin/rinzler:507-516). The C++ parser rejects those forms. The Dice daemon writes the canonical form: slot numbers joined with commas (bin/dice:3656).
rederive.invalid_value: Text that does not parse: 'Dice grant <id>: DICE_SLOTS requested 'invalid'; permitted slot IDs. ...' (src/system/system.cpp:1672) or 'Invalid DICE_SLOTS for Dice grant' (src/system/system.cpp:1504). Slots that do not form one supported instance: 'DICE_SLOTS requested '[...]'; permitted one supported contiguous instance within 0-<last slot>' (src/system/system.cpp:1695-1696), or 'permitted trusted map shapes' (src/system/system.cpp:1703-1704), or 'permitted supported fallback shapes' (src/system/system.cpp:1706-1707). Startup fails in each case.

entries.default: The makefile assigns gen/.fuse_stats_stamp at line 357 for every goal set that has a goal other than list-tests and list-tests-core. A value in the environment is then ignored. When the only goals are list-tests or list-tests-core, the makefile does not assign the name. A value from the environment is then used. Unset there means empty text.
entries.effect: Only when the only goals are list-tests or list-tests-core: make puts the environment value into the prerequisite lists of gen-deb/<package file>, gen/config/core, gen/config/dev, gen/config/test and gen/config/prod while it parses. make does not build those targets for these goals, so a plain path changes no result. A value with make functions, for example $(shell ...), runs those functions during parsing.
entries.name: FUSE_STATS_STAMP
entries.notes: This is an internal make variable, not a documented setting. It is listed because the environment can supply it on the one path where the makefile does not assign it. HAS_AVX512 and TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_REQUIRED have entries for the same reason. list-tests and list-tests-core have no prerequisites (GNUmakefile:1143-1147). Checked with GNU Make 4.3 on a stand-alone copy of the construct outside the checkout: with the goal list-tests the origin of the variable was environment, the value appeared in the prerequisite list, and a $(shell ...) value ran at parse time. With another goal the origin was file. The repository makefile itself was not run. Lowest priority for the document.

doc_mentions.claim: Hugepage precedence: POS_1GB_PER_NUMA scales by the slice count of the instance and takes precedence over POS_NR_HUGEPAGES. Dice preserves the variable for the payload (line 859).
Design doc: the startup hugepage budget (default_n_hugepages = 16) can be overridden by POS_1GB_PER_NUMA, which is sliced by instance. The text points to src/pos/driver.cpp:170-205.
Design doc: the n_hugepages budget is set by default_n_hugepages, POS_NR_HUGEPAGES, POS_1GB_PER_NUMA or ulimit.
Dice preserves POS_NR_HUGEPAGES and POS_1GB_PER_NUMA for runtron and rinzler payloads.

entries.default: Unset: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES is used when it is set. Otherwise the count is the --nr_hugepages value, or 16 hugepages (default_n_hugepages, h/system/config.hpp:12).
entries.effect: Sets how many 1 GiB hugepages the process maps for its DMA heap (the memory that the FPGA cards read and write). With --instance: pages = value x NUMA node count / 8 x slices owned by this instance, in integer arithmetic (src/pos/driver.cpp:260). Without --instance: pages = value.
entries.name: POS_1GB_PER_NUMA
entries.notes: Wins over POS_NR_HUGEPAGES and over --nr_hugepages from the command line or SYSTEM_CONFIG. The NUMA node count in the formula is get_num_numa_nodes(), which counts CPU packages (sockets) in the hwloc topology (src/system/system.cpp:300-307). The divisor 8 is the constant n_slices (h/system/system.hpp:212). The result is capped by the locked-memory limit of the process (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in GiB, src/pos/driver.cpp:277-281). With --instance that limit is first rounded down to a multiple of the slices owned. A negative value becomes a very large unsigned count, which the same cap then lowers to the limit. The comment at src/system/huge.cpp:64-72 names this variable as the one to use in production. When no KV cache size is given, the default KV cache size is half of the hugepage count (src/system/system.cpp:2539-2545). Not read by pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy). doc/dice.md:859 says the Dice daemon passes this variable on to its child processes.

rederive.audience_reason: It sizes the heap memory of deployed rinzler and runtron. The code comment recommends it for production.
rederive.default: Unset: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES is used when it is set. Otherwise the count is the --nr_hugepages value from SYSTEM_CONFIG or the command line, or 16 hugepages (default_n_hugepages, h/system/config.hpp:12).
rederive.disagreement: Not wrong, but vague in two places. 1. The inventory says non-numeric text is read as 0. It does not say that an EMPTY value counts as set: the count becomes 0 and POS_NR_HUGEPAGES is ignored (src/pos/driver.cpp:249, 272). It also does not say what a count of 0 does. 2. cpp-pos-system.json says the default KV cache size is half of the hugepage count. That holds only in the legacy allocator mode. In arena allocator mode the target is inert (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-70). cpp-rinzler-runtron.json has the qualifier.
rederive.effect: Sets how many 1 GiB hugepages the process maps for its DMA heap (the memory that the FPGA cards read and write). With --instance: pages = value x NUMA node count / 8 x slices owned by this instance, in integer arithmetic from left to right (src/pos/driver.cpp:260). Example: value 48, 2 NUMA nodes, an instance with 4 slices: 48 x 2 / 8 x 4 = 48 pages. Without --instance: pages = value (src/pos/driver.cpp:267).
rederive.empty_value: Not the same as unset. An empty value counts as set: atoi gives 0, the page count becomes 0, and POS_NR_HUGEPAGES is not read. A count of 0: by reading the code, the hugepage file is mapped with length 0, the mapping fails, and TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED) stops the process (src/system/huge.cpp:602-605). This was derived by reading. It was not run.
rederive.how_to_check: With --instance, info line 'INIT: hugepages <count> (per numa <value>, per slice <n>)' (src/pos/driver.cpp:261-262). The last number is the number of slices that the instance owns, not pages per slice. Without --instance, debug line 'INIT: using POS_1GB_PER_NUMA without instances configured. hugepages <count>' (src/pos/driver.cpp:268-270). When the cap applies, warning 'INIT: hugepages capped by ulimit constraints to <limit> of <count> available.' (src/pos/driver.cpp:278-279). Debug line 'INIT: Allocating <count> hugepages from <path>* on numa <node>' (src/system/memory.cpp:158-159). With the arena allocator, the FUSE stats file /rinzler/stats/dma_heap/hugepages shows the final budget after the cap (src/system/memory.cpp:634-639). In the legacy allocator mode, with no KV cache size given, 'Trying to use <N> GB for persistent KV cache (covering all models)' prints half of the count (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455-457). The log level is debug when TRON_LOG_LEVEL is unset (src/system/spdlog.cpp:39-42).
rederive.interactions: Wins over POS_NR_HUGEPAGES (else-if at src/pos/driver.cpp:272). Wins over --nr_hugepages from SYSTEM_CONFIG and from the command line, because it is assigned later (order listed at src/system/huge.cpp:61-68). The divisor 8 is the constant n_slices (h/system/system.hpp:212). It is not the slot count of the server. The result is capped by the locked-memory limit of the process (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in GiB, src/pos/driver.cpp:277-281). With --instance that limit is first rounded down to a multiple of the slices owned (src/pos/driver.cpp:264). The packaged rinzler unit sets LimitMEMLOCK=infinity (packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:60). The hugepage count also sets a KV cache default. Legacy allocator mode: with no KV cache size given, the KV cache target is half of the count, in GiB (src/system/system.cpp:2539-2545, src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455-458). The comment at h/system/memory.hpp:69-73 says this can be the count before the cap. Arena allocator mode: that target is made inert (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-70), and the host eviction target defaults to about 95% of the final pool (src/system/memory.cpp:195-205). The comment at src/system/huge.cpp:70 names this variable as the one to use in production. Not read by pos_fake programs.
rederive.invalid_value: Non-numeric text is read as 0. A count of 0: by reading the code, the hugepage file is mapped with length 0, the mapping fails, and TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED) stops the process (src/system/huge.cpp:602-605). This was derived by reading. It was not run. A negative value becomes a very large unsigned count. The memlock cap then lowers it to the limit. There is no error message for a bad value.

doc_mentions.claim: On recent systems the positron service sets the number of hugepages after boot. Set POS_NR_HUGEPAGES to the number of hugepages per NUMA node, for example 48 on a 2-node system for 96 in total.
Set it in /etc/default/positron ("sudo vim /etc/default/positron  # set POS_NR_HUGEPAGES"), then run "sudo systemctl restart positron" (line 67).
Hugepage precedence: POS_1GB_PER_NUMA, then POS_NR_HUGEPAGES, then the count in SYSTEM_CONFIG, then the command-line count. Dice preserves the variable (line 859).
Design doc: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES overrides the startup hugepage budget with an absolute count. The default is default_n_hugepages = 16.
Design doc: the nr_hugepages stat matches the --nr_hugepages option, the n_hugepages global and the POS_NR_HUGEPAGES variable. The budget is fixed at startup.
Design doc table: "Hugepage count, production: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES = 48".
Design doc: set POS_NR_HUGEPAGES=20 for the STORY-425 validation workload. Lines 17, 948 and 1057 repeat the value 20. Line 472 lists the variable as one source of the budget.
Design doc: an MMLU run reached out-of-memory at POS_NR_HUGEPAGES=80. The same run completed with RZ_KV_CACHE_GB=24.

With another goal the origin was file. The repository makefile itself was not run. Lowest priority for the document.

entries.notes: Unit: cores. The check is on bin/bsub-build:27. It calls require_positive_int (bin/bsub-build:19) on the shell variable cores, which already holds the value or the default, so line 27 is not a second read of the environment. rederive.default: Unset: the repository root is worked out from the path of the running program (/proc/self/exe). The last path part named gen or gen-<variant> marks the build tree. If that tree holds a file .checkout-root, its first line is the root. Otherwise the directory above the build tree is the root. A program outside such a tree has an empty root (h/common/paths.hpp:36-76).
rederive.effect: Two effects. 1. Resource map (the YAML file that maps each instance to FPGA cards and CPU cores): <value>/config/resource-map.yaml becomes the third candidate of the search. This applies to every build, also an installed one. 2. FUSE stats mount: in a development build (the program file path contains /gen/), with RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH unset or empty and no --fuse-mount flag, the base mount directory becomes <value>/stats.
rederive.empty_value: Same as unset. The code tests the first character (h/common/paths.hpp:68).
rederive.how_to_check: No log line prints the variable. The resource map in use is logged as 'INIT: Successfully loaded resource map from <path>, server type: <type>' (src/system/system.cpp:1941). The FUSE path in use is logged as 'Stats/config mounted at <path>' (src/rinzler.cpp:4737, src/runtron.cpp:512).
rederive.interactions: Resource map search order: the --resource-map path, resource-map.yaml in the current working directory, <repository root>/config/resource-map.yaml, <program directory>/../config/resource-map.yaml, /opt/positron/config/resource-map.yaml. The first file that loads is used (src/system/resource_map.cpp:84-125). Under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the map is loaded only from /opt/positron/config/resource-map.yaml, so the variable has no effect on the map (src/system/system.cpp:1681, 1930-1934). For the FUSE path, --fuse-mount and RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH come first. A build tree named gen-<variant> does not count as a development build for the FUSE path, because is_dev_build looks for the text /gen/ (h/common/paths.hpp:24-27).
rederive.invalid_value: No check and no error. A wrong path only makes the two derived paths fail later. <value>/config/resource-map.yaml does not load, and the search moves to the next candidate. <value>/stats is created if possible; otherwise the warning 'Could not create FUSE mount point' is logged.

entries.values: JSON text of at most 512 bytes that holds one object. The values in the object must be scalars: nested objects and arrays are rejected. entries.notes: The unit comment (lines 20-25) says /etc/rinzler/instance-<instance>.env, written by platformd, may override the value. README.stats.md:46 says platformd writes RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH=/var/run/rinzler/<N> into that file. /opt/positron/user/config.env is loaded too (line 43). The checkout does not say which of the two files wins when both set the name. rinzler-descriptor runs with set -eu (line 7), so an unset variable stops the script with an error. Inside the binary the --fuse-mount flag wins over the variable (src/rinzler.cpp:4724, src/runtron.cpp:490). When --instance idx,N has N greater than 1, the binary appends /instance-<idx> unless RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED is exactly 1. The repository root of the fallback is REPO_ROOT_OVERRIDE when that variable is set and not empty (h/common/paths.hpp:67). rinzler_proxy is built with RINZLER_NO_FUSE_MOUNT and never mounts, so it ignores this variable (src/rinzler.cpp:129-135, src/CMakeLists.txt:194). packaging/tron-host/README:81-82 says a rinzler_host that a person starts by hand makes its mount in the working directory. The code gives /opt/positron/stats for that case (src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:36), so the README sentence holds only when the working directory is /opt/positron. The last two reader sites are outside this area. Other areas hold more readers and setters (CI workflows, bin/slice, bin/fuse_cleanup.py, bin/ci/benchmark_lib.py, tests).

doc_mentions.claim: Design doc: in arena/governor mode the governor supersedes the static get_kv_cache_size() heuristic and RZ_KV_CACHE_GB. In legacy mode both stay in effect.
Design doc: the token cache target is set once at startup to n_hugepages / 2, and RZ_KV_CACHE_GB can override it.

Design doc: with TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=0 the static sizing path (RZ_KV_CACHE_GB, --kv-cache-gb, --kv-cache-bytes, default n_hugepages / 2) is kept. With TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1 the static knobs are accepted but ignored with one spdlog warning per knob at startup (lines 499-502).
Design doc: the authors know of no RZ_KV_CACHE_GB overrides in production.
Design doc: RZ_KV_CACHE_GB=24 let an MMLU run complete. Lines 1155 and 1165 use the same value in the test plan.
changelog: rinzler: Breaking: size the KV cache by memory use, not RZ_KV_CACHE_GB (#3051).
changelog: rinzler: size the KV cache with --kv-cache-gb or RZ_KV_CACHE_GB (#1387).

entries.default: Unset: the stored size keeps its start value 0xffffffffffffffff (src/system/system.cpp:77). get_kv_cache_size then returns half of the hugepage count, used as a number of GB (src/system/system.cpp:2539). The hugepage count is 16 unless another setting changes it (h/system/config.hpp:12), which gives 8 GB.
entries.effect: Sets the target size of the persistent KV cache (the stored attention keys and values that rinzler keeps between requests). The size covers all models together (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455). rinzler logs 'RZ_KV_CACHE_GB set to <value>' and records that the variable was supplied.
entries.name: RZ_KV_CACHE_GB
entries.notes: Read before the command line is parsed. A --kv-cache-gb system flag is parsed later and writes the same variable, so the flag takes priority (src/system/system.cpp:2046). The flag can come from the command line, or from SYSTEM_CONFIG when the real device library parses it during startup. When the arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) is active, the value is ignored: the cache target is set to the largest int64 value and one warning is logged, 'Arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) is active; ignoring static KV cache sizing knob RZ_KV_CACHE_GB' (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:70 and :86). The arena allocator is the build default (src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86) and TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR selects it at run time. pos_heap_setup, which turns arena mode on, is called only from the real device library (src/pos/driver.cpp:290). rinzler_host, rinzler_mock and rinzler_proxy link the fake device library, so arena mode is never turned on in them (src/system/memory.cpp:286). runtron does not read this variable. runtron has the flags --kv-cache-gb and --kv-cache-bytes (src/runtron.cpp:625). Set outside this area at packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf:19 (value 1). The comment at line 13 of that file gives the default as 8 GB.

entries.values: Whole number of GB. Parsed with std::stoull, base 10 (src/rinzler.cpp:4578). Digits at the start are used and any text after them is ignored. Text that does not start with a number, and an empty value, make std::stoull throw. main has no try block around the call, so the process ends through the terminate handler, which logs a backtrace and calls abort (src/common/backtrace.cpp:33).

entries.values: Unsigned integer, in GB. The code shifts the number left by 30 bits to get bytes (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:458). The text is parsed with std::stoull. An empty or non-numeric value makes std::stoull throw. No try block surrounds the call in main, so the program terminates.

rederive.audience_reason: Memory tuning of a deployed rinzler. A packaged drop-in sets it.
rederive.default: Unset: the stored value keeps the marker 0xffffffffffffffff (src/system/system.cpp:77). get_kv_cache_size then returns half of the hugepage count, used as a number of GiB (src/system/system.cpp:2539-2545). The hugepage count is 16 unless POS_1GB_PER_NUMA, POS_NR_HUGEPAGES or --nr_hugepages changes it (h/system/config.hpp:12), which gives 8 GiB. In arena allocator mode this size is not used (see interactions).
rederive.disagreement: The facts agree. The inventory is vague in two fields. Its 'effect' and 'default' read as if the value always applies. The code ignores the value in arena allocator mode, which is the build default for the real rinzler (src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86, src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-88). The inventory says this only in 'notes'. Two details are missing: the unit is GiB (shift by 30 bits, src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:458), and the value -1 wraps to the 'not set' marker, so the default applies.
rederive.effect: Only in legacy allocator mode: sets the target size of the persistent KV cache (the stored attention keys and values that rinzler keeps between requests). One target covers all models together. In arena allocator mode the value is ignored and a warning is logged.
rederive.empty_value: Not the same as unset. rinzler logs 'RZ_KV_CACHE_GB set to '. std::stoull then throws std::invalid_argument. main has no try block around the call. The terminate handler logs a backtrace and calls abort (src/common/backtrace.cpp:33-36, installed at src/rinzler.cpp:4548).
rederive.how_to_check: 'RZ_KV_CACHE_GB set to <text>' at startup (src/rinzler.cpp:4577) shows the raw text. 'Trying to use <N> GB for persistent KV cache (covering all models)' (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:456) shows the number when the cache object is created. That line is also printed in arena mode, where the number is then not used. The warning 'Arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) is active; ignoring static KV cache sizing knob RZ_KV_CACHE_GB' (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:76-80) shows that the value is ignored.
rederive.interactions: 1. Arena allocator mode (pos_heap_v2) ignores the value. The cache target is set to the largest int64 value and one warning is logged (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-88). Arena mode is the build default (option TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON is ON, src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86), and TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR selects the mode at run time (src/system/memory.cpp:93-97). The mode is set in pos_heap_setup, which only the real device library calls (src/pos/driver.cpp:290). So on a default build of rinzler the variable has no effect unless TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR holds a value other than 1. In rinzler_host, rinzler_mock and rinzler_proxy arena mode stays off. rinzler_host contains the token cache code (fake_scheduler_static, src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:431-433), so the value is used there. rinzler_mock and rinzler_proxy read and store the value, but their scheduler libraries do not contain the token cache code (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:440-452), and I found no user of the value in them. 2. The flag --kv-cache-gb is parsed later and writes the same variable, so the flag wins (src/system/system.cpp:2046-2048). The flag can be on the command line. For the real rinzler it can also be inside SYSTEM_CONFIG. 3. runtron has the flags --kv-cache-gb and --kv-cache-bytes instead (src/runtron.cpp:625-636). 4. The host package drop-in sets the value 1 (packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf:19).
rederive.invalid_value: Text that does not start with a number ends the process the same way as an empty value. A number too large for 64 bits throws std::out_of_range, with the same result.
rederive.name: RZ_KV_CACHE_GB

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy (all four compile src/rinzler.cpp, src/CMakeLists.txt:95, 115, 152, 180). runtron does not read it

rederive.values: A whole number of GiB. The code shifts the number left by 30 bits to get bytes (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:458). Parsed with std::stoull, base 10 (src/rinzler.cpp:4578). Leading white space and a + or - sign are accepted. Parsing stops at the first character that is not a digit, so 8GB gives 8 and 1.5 gives 1. 0 gives a target of 0 bytes. -1 wraps to 0xffffffffffffffff, which is the internal marker for 'not set', so the default size applies. I checked these std::stoull results with a stand-alone test program on this host.

Set RZ_RUNFILE_DIR to a writable directory (unset or empty means /var/log/positron).' The run file is JSON with the pid, the model names, and the instance id and total (src/rinzler.cpp:2490). The path of the write is kept and used again for the removal (src/rinzler.cpp:2517). t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py:42 repeats the default in Python (outside this area).

doc_mentions.claim: RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1 turns a server into a tokenizer: a save_tokens request gets a 200 with only the save_tokens object and nothing is generated. Read once at startup. Unset or 0 is off. Any value other than 0 or 1 fails startup. 1 together with RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0 also fails startup (lines 163-164).
Environment table: read at rinzler.cpp startup, shared with production rinzler. 1 answers save_tokens requests before generation. Unset or 0 is off. Anything else fails startup.
Capture golden tokens from a server that does not have RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1, because a prompt-only capture has an empty output_tokens.
Trace span dictionary: with RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1 the "Stream generate" span opens and closes, and no callback, detokenization or response spans follow.
changelog: rinzler: add RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY for prompt-only captures (#5162).

entries.default: Unset: off. save_tokens requests run a normal generation.
entries.effect: A request with save_tokens true is answered before generation. The response holds only the save_tokens capture data. No tokens are generated. The code comments call this the tokenizer sidecar mode (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:299).

With the value 1 rinzler logs 'save_tokens requests answer before generation (RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1)'. Requests without save_tokens still generate normally (src/rinzler.cpp:3647).

doc_mentions.claim: RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE=YYYY-MM-DD pins the render date of both chat renderers: the Harmony conversation_start_date and the strftime_now clock of the HF Jinja path. The value is validated at startup.
Environment table: read at rinzler.cpp startup, shared with production rinzler. It must equal the rendered_at entry of the golden file when one is declared, or every generation throws.
The proxy checks the pair on every generation: a golden file that declares rendered_at throws unless RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE matches (fix shown on line 122).
launch_proxy in t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp reads rendered_at from the golden file and exports RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE into the child process.
Capture recipe: set it on the capture server before requesting save_tokens. An unpinned capture records the local date of that day.
A tokenizer sidecar must be launched with the same RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE as the serving host. Line 214: a legacy-completions golden file needs no pinned date. Line 102 is the section heading.
Set RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE=YYYY-MM-DD on the capture server. launch.py re-exports the recorded date so that the replayed proxy renders the same key (lines 521-522). Example on line 209.
changelog: rinzler: pin prompt dates via RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE or date_string (#3574).

entries.default: Unset: no pinned date. rinzler uses today's local date and computes it again for each request. Empty value: fails the format check, so startup fails.
entries.effect: Pins the date that rinzler writes into prompts. The 'Current date' line of the Harmony (gpt-oss) system message uses the value (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:1085). The strftime_now function of Hugging Face chat templates uses local noon of that date (src/rinzler/hf-token-processor.cpp:680). The rendered_at field of a save_tokens capture reports it.
entries.name: RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE
entries.notes: On a bad value rinzler logs 'RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE validation failed: ...' and exits with code 1 (src/rinzler.cpp:2387). The comment at src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:842 says the variable mirrors VLLM_SYSTEM_START_DATE of vLLM for the Harmony path. Nothing in the checkout reads VLLM_SYSTEM_START_DATE. Chat templates that never call strftime_now are not affected (comment at h/rinzler/chat-template-reserved-keys.hpp:16). In rinzler_proxy the proxy scheduler reads the variable again for every generation. It throws std::runtime_error when the golden file declares a rendered_at date and the variable is unset or holds a different text (src/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.cpp:229 and :236). The pinned date is turned into a time with mktime, and dates are formatted with localtime_r, so the time zone (TZ) applies.

rederive.audience_reason: It changes how much a deployed rinzler or runtron logs.
rederive.default: Unset: the logger keeps the level from TRON_LOG_LEVEL. That level is debug when TRON_LOG_LEVEL is unset (src/system/spdlog.cpp:39-43).
rederive.disagreement: Both inventory entries say 'not determined' for the accepted values, for the default, and for how the logger level combines with the output levels. spdlog 1.17.0 is the version that cmake/versions.cmake:5 pins. Its source says: a comma list of LEVEL or NAME=LEVEL; level names trace, debug, info, warning or warn, error or err, critical, off; case is ignored; an empty value is the same as unset; an unknown level name is ignored silently. The variable changes only the logger level. The outputs keep the TRON_LOG_LEVEL level, so the variable can only reduce logging. The example console=err in the code comment matches no TRON logger.
rederive.effect: Changes the level of TRON's logger after TRON_LOG_LEVEL has been applied. It does not change the level of the two outputs (stderr and the log file). They keep the TRON_LOG_LEVEL level (src/system/spdlog.cpp:47, 50). A message is written only if it passes the logger level and also the output level (spdlog include/spdlog/logger.h:262, logger-inl.h:135-137). So SPDLOG_LEVEL can only reduce logging. Example: SPDLOG_LEVEL=warn hides info and debug lines. SPDLOG_LEVEL=trace alone shows nothing more, because the outputs stay at debug.
rederive.empty_value: Same as unset (spdlog include/spdlog/cfg/env.h:30).
rederive.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the level in effect. The only sign is which levels appear in the output.
rederive.interactions: TRON_LOG_LEVEL sets the logger level and both output levels first. To get more detail, set TRON_LOG_LEVEL. SPDLOG_LEVEL=off stops all log output, errors included. The entry console=err from the code comment at src/system/spdlog.cpp:59 matches no logger in TRON, so it does nothing. The test launcher of rinzler_proxy removes the variable from the child environment (t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp:1123).
rederive.invalid_value: An entry with an unknown level name is ignored, with no message. The other entries still apply. Text of 32768 characters or more is ignored as a whole (spdlog include/spdlog/cfg/helpers-inl.h:74, 88).
rederive.name: SPDLOG_LEVEL

rederive.values: A comma-separated list. Each entry is either LEVEL, which sets the global level, or NAME=LEVEL, which sets the level of the logger called NAME. LEVEL is one of trace, debug, info, warning (or warn), error (or err), critical, off. Upper and lower case are both accepted. Spaces around names are removed. TRON creates one logger, named default_logger (src/system/spdlog.cpp:53-54).

conflicts: All areas agree on the product parser. The readers differ in how much of the text they understand, and the document should say so. rinzler and runtron parse every system option (src/system/system.cpp:1954-2052). The Python wrappers, bin/slice, bin/dice and the LSF bridge understand only --instance X,Y and --instance=X,Y, and bin/slice also a bare X,Y. Three test-side parsers do not understand the joined form --instance=X,Y: t/t_rinzler.cpp:137-139 and t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp:1004-1008 use sscanf with '--instance %d,%d', and t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py:54-60 compares a whole word with --instance. Their defaults also differ: 0,4 in t_rinzler, 0,1 in t_rinzler_proxy and in the proxy harness. The audience test in python-rest describes only the harness reader; the audience of the name is operator.

doc_mentions.claim: Performance parameters (devices, hugepages, NUMA, CPU pinning) can be given on the runtron command line or in the SYSTEM_CONFIG environment variable, which runtron and "libalderaan" read (line 569). The value holds the same options as the command line: --optimize, --no-opt, --devices, --app-cores, --dev-cores, --numa, --nr_hugepages, --hugepage_file, --instance id,max (lines 571-579). Line 586: the system uses the union of command line and environment variable, and the environment variable wins a conflict.
Example: export SYSTEM_CONFIG="--numa 0 --devices \"21:00.0\" --app-cores \"1-5\" --dev-cores \"6,7\"".
changelog: runtime: read options from the SYSTEM_CONFIG environment variable (#348).
Test rule: honor SYSTEM_CONFIG=--instance i,n and derive child instances with get_sub_instances().
launch_proxy in t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp forwards --instance <id>,<n> from SYSTEM_CONFIG to rinzler_proxy.
SYSTEM_CONFIG="--instance 0,2" limits a Slice run to one instance.
A test asks for a number of slices through SYSTEM_CONFIG=--instance <iid>,<n_instances>. Line 132: the "inst x,y" column of the Slice report matches it.
Slice starts each test with TRON_LOG_DIR, SYSTEM_CONFIG and RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH set. The log header example on line 143 shows SYSTEM_CONFIG='--instance 1,8'.
Placement stays strict when the caller supplied SYSTEM_CONFIG. Line 345: a manual full refresh needs a whole-box allocation, not a subset SYSTEM_CONFIG.
Wrapper knob table: "--instance X,Y" slot request. The default is the whole box. Serving wrappers keep the other tuning fields while Dice supplies the granted instance.

The Dice daemon sets SYSTEM_CONFIG=--instance X,Y for the dispatched subprocess when the grant is an aligned partition. In shared mode the value comes from the grant and is not merged with the incoming SYSTEM_CONFIG of the submitter (line 620).

In shared Dice, --instance X,Y or SYSTEM_CONFIG is a hard boundary. Children also receive SYSTEM_CONFIG when the grant can be written as --instance X,Y (line 440). Lines 358, 444, 593, 596 and 608 repeat the boundary rule.
Remote placement table: unset or --instance 0,1 is the whole box, --instance 0,2 is the NUMA 0 half, --instance 1,2 is the NUMA 1 half. Examples on lines 140 and 147.
"bin/slice submit" honors SYSTEM_CONFIG. Line 327: --instance X,Y follows the SYSTEM_CONFIG convention, instance X of Y covers slots [X*(8/Y), (X+1)*(8/Y)).

entries.name: SYSTEM_CONFIG
entries.notes: 1. Second use: rinzler and runtron call early_parse_instance at program start (src/rinzler.cpp:4563, src/runtron.cpp:489). That call reads --instance from this variable only when the command line has no --instance (src/system/system.cpp:1024-1027). rinzler uses the result for the log line prefix and for the FUSE stats mount directory. runtron uses it for the FUSE stats mount directory. 2. A bad value makes system_parse_env return false. pos_startup_host then logs 'INIT: invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG' and returns -1. With the real driver, get_devices then exits the process with status 1 (src/pos/driver.cpp:887-889). Causes: --instance not in the form x,y, two --instance options, an empty or badly formed device list (each entry has the form e1:00.0: three hexadecimal numbers of 1 or 2 digits, src/system/system.cpp:323-343), an empty CPU list, an option that needs a value at the end of the text. 3. Numbers have no error handling. The values of --numa, --nr_hugepages, --tracer-core and --kv-cache-gb are parsed with std::stoi or std::stoull (src/system/system.cpp:2022-2047). Non-numeric text there throws a C++ exception, and pos_startup_host is noexcept (src/pos/driver.cpp:191), so the process ends. The numbers inside CPU lists are parsed with std::stoi inside parse_cpu_list, which is itself noexcept (src/system/system.cpp:388-405). Non-numeric text in a CPU list therefore ends the process on every path, also when the option comes from the command line. Under a Dice grant a bad CPU list is rejected earlier with a 'Dice grant' error (dice_cpu_list, src/system/system.cpp:1561-1582). 4. Each parse outside a Dice grant reloads the resource map (src/system/system.cpp:1935). The path for that reload comes only from the text being parsed. So when SYSTEM_CONFIG is set and does not repeat --resource-map, a --resource-map from the command line is dropped and the default search order is used. 5. The hugepage count from --nr_hugepages is replaced later by POS_1GB_PER_NUMA or POS_NR_HUGEPAGES, and --hugepage_file by POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH (src/pos/driver.cpp:249-288). 6. Under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the command line and this variable are checked together against the granted slots before any option is applied. The --instance here must equal the instance that DICE_SLOTS describes (src/system/system.cpp:2086-2102). 7. Setter sites listed are examples from outside this area. The regular-expression scan of the checkout lists 30 setter sites.

rederive.audience_reason: It selects which FPGA cards, CPU cores and memory a deployed rinzler or runtron uses.
rederive.default: Unset: nothing is read from the environment, and only the system options from the command line apply. Exception: with DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1 an unset value fails startup, because --instance is then required (src/pos/driver.cpp:209-224).
rederive.disagreement: The two inventory files contradict each other on one reader. cpp-pos-system.json names rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host as programs that reach the read at src/pos/fake.cpp:99. cpp-rinzler-runtron.json says they do not reach it. The code agrees with cpp-rinzler-runtron.json: only pos_startup (src/pos/fake.cpp:147) calls the fake pos_startup_host, no file under src/ or h/ calls pos_startup for the fake library, and the fake get_devices is a stub (src/pos/fake.cpp:398). Only tests reach src/pos/fake.cpp:99. So in those three programs, options other than --instance inside SYSTEM_CONFIG have no effect outside a Dice grant. Both files also omit the log line 'INIT: environment system config: <text>' (src/pos/driver.cpp:210), which shows the parsed text. All other facts agree.
rederive.effect: Gives system placement options to the process through the environment. --instance selects the share of the server (FPGA cards, CPU cores, NUMA node, hugepage files) that the process owns. The real device library parses the whole text during startup, after the command line was parsed. rinzler and runtron also read only the --instance value at program start, when the command line has none. rinzler uses it for the log line label rz<X>/<Y>. rinzler and runtron use it for the /instance-<X> part of the FUSE stats path.
rederive.empty_value: Outside a Dice grant: parsed as an empty option list. The line 'INIT: environment system config: ' is logged and no option changes. One difference from unset: the resource map is loaded again, so a --resource-map given only on the command line is no longer the loaded map (see interactions). Under a Dice grant: startup fails, as for unset.
rederive.how_to_check: 'INIT: environment system config: <text>' at info level (src/pos/driver.cpp:210, src/pos/fake.cpp:101) shows the text that was parsed. 'Configured instance X,Y using resource map (<path>).' or 'Configured instance X,Y using hardcoded settings.' (src/system/system.cpp:1986-1990) shows the instance in effect. Without an instance: 'INIT: No --instance specified, applying system_optimize() defaults.' (src/system/system.cpp:2065). rinzler log lines carry the label rzX/Y (src/system/spdlog.cpp:86). The rinzler run file holds the instance id and total (src/rinzler.cpp:2491).
rederive.interactions: 1. Order: the command line is parsed first and SYSTEM_CONFIG second. For an option present in both, the SYSTEM_CONFIG value is applied last. 2. POS_1GB_PER_NUMA or POS_NR_HUGEPAGES replace --nr_hugepages afterwards, and POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH replaces --hugepage_file (src/pos/driver.cpp:249-288). 3. Each parse outside a Dice grant loads the resource map again, and the path comes only from the text being parsed (src/system/system.cpp:1911-1936). So when SYSTEM_CONFIG is set and has no --resource-map, a --resource-map from the command line is replaced by the default search. 4. If the command line and SYSTEM_CONFIG both carry --instance with different values, the placement follows SYSTEM_CONFIG, but the log label and the FUSE suffix follow the command line (src/system/system.cpp:1024-1027). This point is read from the code and was not run. 5. Under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the command line and SYSTEM_CONFIG are checked together against DICE_SLOTS before anything is applied. --instance must equal the granted instance. The form --option=value is then accepted for every option that takes a value (src/system/system.cpp:1869-1905, 2086-2102). 6. rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host do not run the full parse, because the fake get_devices is a stub (src/pos/fake.cpp:398) and no product code calls pos_startup with the fake library. Outside a Dice grant they use only the --instance value: for the log label, and in rinzler_mock and rinzler_host also for the FUSE suffix. Options such as --kv-cache-gb inside SYSTEM_CONFIG have no effect in these three programs. 7. In the real rinzler, --kv-cache-gb here overrides RZ_KV_CACHE_GB. 8. Dice, Slice and the wrappers bin/rinzler and bin/runtron set the variable for the programs they start.
rederive.invalid_value: Three different results. 1. Clean failure. A wrong --instance form, two --instance options, a bad device list, an empty CPU list, or a missing value at the end of the text make the parse return false. pos_startup_host logs 'INIT: invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG', and get_devices exits the process with code 1 (src/pos/driver.cpp:211-215, 887-889). 2. Process end without that message. Non-numeric text for --numa, --nr_hugepages, --tracer-core or --kv-cache-gb, or inside a CPU list, throws a C++ exception inside a noexcept function, so the process is terminated (src/system/system.cpp:388-405, 2022-2047; src/pos/driver.cpp:191). 3. Silent. A token that is not a known option is ignored with no message, for example a misspelled option or --numa=0.

rederive.audience_reason: Needed to load gpt-oss models on a host that cannot download, or to avoid the shared cache.
rederive.default: Unset: the library uses a cache directory. The cache directory is $TIKTOKEN_RS_CACHE_DIR when that is set, otherwise <temporary directory>/tiktoken-rs-cache. A cached file with the right hash is used. Otherwise the library downloads https://openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net/encodings/o200k_base.tiktoken into the cache and checks the hash (openai-harmony src/tiktoken_ext/public_encodings.rs:128-137, 417-441, 462-479). A host with no cached file and no internet access cannot load a gpt-oss model.
rederive.disagreement: The inventory is right but vague on three points. 1. It does not say what an empty value does: the variable counts as set, and the file is looked for in the current working directory. 2. It does not say that a set variable disables the download fallback, so a missing file or a wrong hash fails the model load. 3. It does not say where the cache is when the variable is unset ($TIKTOKEN_RS_CACHE_DIR or <temporary directory>/tiktoken-rs-cache), or that a cold cache needs internet access. Its evidence can also be stronger: rust/harmony/Cargo.lock:1343 pins the exact commit that I read.
rederive.effect: Makes the Harmony tokenizer library read its vocabulary file from the given directory, with a hash check. The download and the shared cache are then not used.
rederive.empty_value: Not the same as unset. Rust std::env::var returns the empty text, so the variable counts as set. The library then opens o200k_base.tiktoken in the current working directory of the process and tries no download. This is read from the library source and was not run.
rederive.how_to_check: none found on success. On failure, the error text 'Failed to load Harmony encoding ...' names the cause.
rederive.interactions: It matters only when a model whose execution slug contains gpt-oss is loaded. When it is unset, TIKTOKEN_RS_CACHE_DIR and the temporary directory decide where the cache is. bin/slice fetches the file one time and sets the variable for the tests it starts (bin/slice:1844-1876). The packaged rinzler unit does not set it. All facts here depend on the library version. rust/harmony/Cargo.toml:13 pins tag v0.0.8, and rust/harmony/Cargo.lock:1343 pins commit ec7606df9e87e3d0a1fec9f50928c1e407f0c438. Check again when the pin moves (bin/slice:1750-1753 says the same).
rederive.invalid_value: When the variable is set, the library does not fall back to the download. A missing file, an unreadable file or a wrong hash makes the load fail. The harmony_encoding constructor throws harmony_error 'Failed to load Harmony encoding 'HarmonyGptOss': Failed to load encoding: invalid tiktoken vocab file: ...' (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:220, rust/harmony/src/lib.rs:477). I found no try block around the construction in load_model or around the controller construction in main (src/rinzler.cpp:2137, 4994), so the process ends through the terminate handler. This is read from the code and was not run.

Python code in this area calls tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() without a directory 34 times (31 in config/test_model_definitions.py, 1 each in perfetto/test_perfetto.py:42, ingest/runtime/scripts/gemma3_rmsnorm_contract_test.py:109 and ingest/runtime/tests/test_ingest_runner.py:24) and tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile 11 times (config/test_model_definitions.py). The Python standard library chooses the directory for those calls; the checkout does not state which variables it reads. The two tempfile.mkstemp calls pass dir= and do not use the default directory (config/model_definitions.py:84, ingest/export/reference_logits.py:33). Confidence is low only because the reader default is not determined; the set site is certain.

setters.why: the tests check that the launchers leave no temporary file behind

entries.name: TMPDIR
entries.notes: Many scripts of this area call mktemp without naming a directory, for example ci-bundle-artifact.sh line 38 and test/deb-package-contents.sh lines 35 to 38. GNU mktemp then creates the file under TMPDIR, or under /tmp when TMPDIR is unset. That is mktemp behaviour, measured with GNU coreutils 8.32 outside the checkout. No script names TMPDIR for it. ci-shared-nfs.sh always gives mktemp a full path, so TMPDIR has no effect there.

doc_mentions.claim: On SIGUSR1 a process traces to tron::perfetto_trace_dest, which defaults to "traced" (the system backend). Setting TRACE_FILE=/path switches to the in-process backend: the process writes that file itself and ignores the .cfg file. Use it only for a capture without the daemons (line 212).
The TRACE_FILE variable sets tron::perfetto_trace_dest in pos_startup_host() (src/pos/driver.cpp). The default is "traced".
With TRACE_FILE set to a path, a SIGUSR1 capture lasts the 10 s window. Line 67: for an external capture leave TRACE_FILE unset or set it to "traced".

With TRACE_FILE unset or "traced", the SIGUSR1 tracer joins a traced session, and a set TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES then ends rinzler. With TRACE_FILE naming a path, the capture records in-process and TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES applies (line 301). Line 269 lists this case.
The in-process file backend used by --trace FILE, --trace-gen FILE and TRACE_FILE enables the periodic file writer with the 5,000 ms default of Perfetto v57.2.
With TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES set and TRACE_FILE unset or "traced", the SIGUSR1 of perfetto/wrapper ends rinzler.
rinzler-capture.sh refuses a rinzler started with a TRACE_FILE other than "traced".
In-process captures from TRACE_FILE read the buffer statistics during capture, so the last snapshot can predate the end of the trace.
changelog: tracing: honor TRACE_FILE for traces started by SIGUSR1 (#3790).
changelog: tracing: write a Perfetto trace from libtron when TRACE_FILE is set (#563).

entries.default: Unset: the trace destination stays traced (src/pos/perf.cpp:34). traced is the Perfetto system daemon. An outside client owns the session.
entries.effect: Sets the process-wide Perfetto trace destination. A SIGUSR1 capture (a 10 second trace that the process starts when it receives signal SIGUSR1, src/pos/perf.cpp:248-291) then writes to that file from inside the process, instead of sending events to the traced daemon.
entries.name: TRACE_FILE
entries.notes: The file is opened with O_TRUNC and mode 0600 at each capture (src/pos/perf.cpp:173-175), so a new capture replaces the old file. If the file cannot be opened, start_tracing throws inside a noexcept thread and the process ends. An empty value fails the same way (comment at perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:202-205). The failure happens at the SIGUSR1 signal, not at startup. Only programs with the real driver install the SIGUSR1 tracer (src/pos/driver.cpp:447), and only they read this variable. runtron --trace and --trace-gen write the same global earlier, before the model run starts (src/runtron.cpp:263, 295), and the runtron trace takes its destination at that point (src/runtron.cpp:267, 342). pos_startup_host runs later, at the first get_devices call, and then this variable replaces the global. So in runtron the variable changes only the destination of later SIGUSR1 captures. That order was read from src/runtron.cpp, which belongs to another area. README.perfetto.md:206-212 describes the variable. Two tests read the same name with their own getenv (t/t_gof_staging_leaks.cpp:74, t/t_pos_lifecycle_fake.cpp:200). Those files belong to another sweep. No setter was found in the checkout.

rederive.audience_reason: It is for performance trace capture, not for normal serving. A wrong value can end the process at SIGUSR1.
rederive.default: Unset: the destination stays traced (src/pos/perf.cpp:34). traced means the Perfetto system backend: the process only registers as a producer, and an outside client (perfetto/wrapper or perfetto/tronperf) owns the session and the output file (note at h/common/perfetto.hpp:223-241).
rederive.effect: Sets the process-wide Perfetto trace destination. With a file path, a capture started by the signal SIGUSR1 (10 seconds long) is recorded inside the process and written to that file. The file is opened with O_CREAT and O_TRUNC, mode 0600, at each capture, so each new capture replaces the last one.
rederive.empty_value: Not the same as unset. The destination becomes the empty text. Nothing happens at startup. At the first SIGUSR1 the open of an empty path fails, start_tracing throws inside a noexcept thread function, and the process is terminated (src/pos/perf.cpp:173-175, 248, 273).
rederive.how_to_check: 'INIT: perfetto trace destination: <text>' at startup, only when the variable is set (src/pos/driver.cpp:229). At each SIGUSR1: 'perfetto tracing starting (<destination>)' at warning level (src/pos/perf.cpp:269).
rederive.interactions: 1. TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES. With TRACE_FILE unset or traced and TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES non-empty, a SIGUSR1 capture throws and ends the process (src/pos/perf.cpp:126-134, 165). With a file path, TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES selects the categories (src/pos/perf.cpp:143-149). 2. runtron --trace and --trace-gen write the same global before the device library starts and pass their own destination to their trace session (src/runtron.cpp:263-267, 295, 342). pos_startup_host runs later and overwrites the global when TRACE_FILE is set. So in runtron the variable changes only later SIGUSR1 captures. This order is read from the code and was not run. 3. rinzler ignores a SIGUSR1 that arrives during a FUSE capture (src/pos/perf.cpp:264-267). 4. Only programs with the real device library read the variable and install the SIGUSR1 tracer (src/pos/driver.cpp:447). rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host do not. 5. perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh refuses a target rinzler whose TRACE_FILE is not traced (perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:208-209).
rederive.invalid_value: A path that cannot be opened for writing gives the same result as an empty value: no error at startup, and process end at the first SIGUSR1.

rederive.audience_reason: The source calls it a switch for emergency disable and rollback of the AMX path (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:86, h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:47-50), and the packaged deb build contains it.
rederive.default: Unset: the probe runs. It checks CPUID leaf 7 EDX bits 22 and 24, XCR0 bits 17 and 18, and asks Linux for the tile permission with arch_prctl (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:90-98). The AMX kernel is used when all three pass.
rederive.effect: available() returns false for the whole process. Software attention then uses the AVX-512 loop for every KV page. The AMX kernel serves only models with head size 128 and 4 query heads per KV head on an executor that stores bf16 (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:149-166), so the variable changes nothing for other models.
rederive.empty_value: Same as unset. The empty text is not equal to 1.
rederive.how_to_check: No log line prints the value. The FUSE stats file /model/<model id>/attention/summary has the fields amx_compiled and amx_available (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:727-731; filled at h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:478-479). amx_compiled true with amx_available false means that the variable is 1 or that the host has no usable AMX. The file exists also when TRON_ATTN_STATS is off (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:934), but only when FUSE stats are initialized (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:916). With TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 the same summary is printed to stderr when the model state is destroyed (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:829-830).
rederive.interactions: The read exists only in a build with the CMake option TRON_AMX_DISPATCH. The option is OFF by default (CMakeLists.txt:46). It is ON in the deb preset (CMakePresets.json:68) and in the CMake CI job (.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:355). In a build without the option the variable is never read. There is no command-line flag. The value cannot change while the process runs.
rederive.invalid_value: Any text other than 1 (for example 0, true, yes, or 1 with a space) is ignored. No message is logged. AMX stays on.

rederive.effect: When the value is above 0, every extend request first calls defrag_books(value) on the token tree node that it extends (src/tron/scheduler/full.cpp:121). The call takes the node and up to value - 1 ancestors. From the oldest to the youngest, it tries to move the KV book of each node into the free end of the book of its parent (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1321-1342 and :1473-1500). A move happens only when the node starts its own book, the parent book ends where the node starts, and the parent book has room.

Each call that passes the early returns reserves memory for value pointers of 8 bytes each (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1331), so a very large value costs memory on every extend request. This happens at the first extend request from a node whose parent is not the root, because the early returns at h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1325-1329 come first. Verification prunes the tree to TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE nodes (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:695-696), so with the default size 2 only one drafted node is verified, whatever the width is. doc_mentions.claim: Design doc: TRON_HEAP_SHADOW (or the --heap-shadow flag), if set, makes the arena allocator keep a per-allocation shadow map for exact size checks on deallocate and for dump_profile. Off by default. The setting is latched in the pos_heap_v2 constructor, resolved in pos_heap_setup() before the first allocation, and fixed for the life of the heap (lines 782-789). It replaces the HEAP_V2_SHADOW CMake option.
Design doc: the shadow map operations are guarded by a flag latched from TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1 (or --heap-shadow). It cannot be toggled during a run.
Design doc phase list: convert HEAP_V2_SHADOW to runtime gating through TRON_HEAP_SHADOW or --heap-shadow.
Design doc history: shadow tracking is enabled per process by TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1 or --heap-shadow before the first allocation. It is off by default.

rederive.effect: Sets the smallest minibatch size that uses the early launch of hardware attention. A minibatch with at least this many token jobs prepares and launches hardware attention before the K/V saves of the current token. A smaller minibatch saves K/V first and then prepares and launches (Note at h/tron/models/model.hpp:95-109, select_hw_attention_launch_phase at h/tron/models/model.hpp:159-163). The value 1 means always early. A value above every batch size means always late.

rederive.how_to_check: No log line prints the value. Perfetto trace instant events of the category hwattention-detail (early_hw_attn_prepare, early_hw_attn, late_hw_attn_prepare, late_hw_attn) carry the argument min_b with the value in effect (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2467-2469, :2580-2582, :2595-2597, :2614-2616).
rederive.interactions: It selects only the launch time. It cannot make a software-only operation use hardware (h/tron/models/model.hpp:107-109). It matters only for operations that run on hardware attention. No command-line flag sets it.
rederive.invalid_value: TRON_ASSERT at h/tron/models/model.hpp:121-125 fails. The process writes the error log line 'TRON_ASSERT(...): invalid TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B '<value>'; expected a positive integer', then 'Aborting.', and calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:59-63). Rejected inputs: empty text, a sign (+4, -1), a space, a letter, 0, and a number above the 64-bit range. The check runs at the first use. The first use is in a forward pass, when the first attention job is prepared (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2460-2461). It is not at program start. So a program with a bad value starts, loads the model, and aborts later.

EMEM is the FPGA memory that holds the Q.K dot products of hardware attention (h/libpos.hpp:128-130). With the flag off, such a pass is split into several commands. entries.effect: Sets the soft limit on the number of live tokens (token jobs) that one forward pass of a scheduler takes. At the limit the scheduler stops adding tokens to the pass and records that the pass did not schedule everything.
entries.name: TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT
entries.notes: When the model config has max_minibatches above 0, the limit is lowered to max_minibatches x max_minibatch_size. The field comment calls it a soft limit that can be exceeded in some cases (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1976): a page that already has KV work is bound only by the hard capacity limit (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2180-2188). The variable is read each time a scheduler is constructed; an EAGLE draft scheduler is a second scheduler and reads it again. The code does not reject 0 or a negative value. The check 'n_live_tokens >= live_token_limit' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2410) is then true for the first token of every edge, so that loop adds no token to the pass. bin/analyze-tps puts the assignment in front of the runtron command that it runs on a remote host.

rederive.default: Unset: 100000000 tokens (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1838). This is in practice no limit.
rederive.disagreement: Vague on the outcome of a bad value. cpp-tron.json says that with 0 or a negative value 'that loop adds no token to the pass' and stops there. The code goes on: build_forward_plan returns false with no token job, and forward() fails TRON_ASSERT 'Scheduler stuck: no work scheduled but not finished' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2020-2025). So an empty value, non-numeric text, 0 or a negative number aborts the process at the first forward pass that has a token to schedule. The document must state this. Parsing, default and effect agree.
rederive.effect: Sets the soft limit on the number of live tokens that one forward pass of a scheduler takes. At the limit the tree walk stops adding tokens to the pass (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2410-2413). The first K/V token of a page and a listener-only token are admitted only below the limit (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2191, :2543). A lower value gives smaller forward passes and more of them.
rederive.empty_value: atoi gives 0. The result is the same as for an invalid value: the process aborts at the first forward pass that has work.
rederive.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the limit. The Perfetto instant event 'forward args' of the category scheduler shows the number of token jobs of each pass (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2071-2074), which stays at or near the limit under load.
rederive.interactions: When max_minibatches of the model config is above 0, the limit is the smaller of the variable and max_minibatches x max_minibatch_size (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1839-1842). max_minibatches comes from rinzler -b / --max-batches (src/rinzler.cpp:4323-4325) or runtron --max-minibatches (src/runtron.cpp:969), merged with a bound from the model plugin (h/tron/models/config.hpp:112-118). The limit is soft: a page that already has K/V work is bound only by the hard capacity limit (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2181-2189). Each scheduler reads the variable when it is built. An EAGLE draft scheduler is a second scheduler and reads it again. rederive.audience_reason: It sets the amount of log output of every deployed TRON program, and a wrong name turns all log output off.
rederive.default: Unset: debug (src/system/spdlog.cpp:40-42).
rederive.disagreement: Vague. Both inventory files say the accepted names and the result of an unknown name were 'not determined', and that the way spdlog combines logger level and sink level was not determined. spdlog v1.17.0 answers all three. (1) The accepted names are trace, debug, info, warning, error, critical and off, plus warn and err. The match is exact and case-sensitive. (2) Any other text, the empty text included, gives the level off. The process then writes no log message at all, not even errors. (3) SPDLOG_LEVEL changes only the logger level. The sinks keep the TRON_LOG_LEVEL level. The stricter of the two wins. Source: spdlog v1.17.0, read from a local build copy at /home/jhan/workspace/tron/gen/_deps/spdlog-src (its version.h reports 1.17.0). The checkout pins v1.17.0 at cmake/versions.cmake:5 but does not hold the spdlog source. The default (debug) and the read time agree.
rederive.effect: Sets the lowest message level that TRON writes. The level is applied to the log file sink, to the stderr sink and to the default logger (src/system/spdlog.cpp:47, :50, :55).
rederive.empty_value: The empty text is not a level name, so the level is off. No message is written to stderr or to the log file.
rederive.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the level in effect. A debug line such as the per-card 'caps { ... }' line (src/pos/device.cpp:337) appears only at debug or trace.
rederive.interactions: SPDLOG_LEVEL is applied after it (src/system/spdlog.cpp:60). In spdlog v1.17.0, load_env_levels changes only the level of the logger. The two sinks keep the level from TRON_LOG_LEVEL, and a message must pass both the logger level and the sink level. So the stricter of the two variables wins. SPDLOG_LEVEL can hide more messages but cannot show more than TRON_LOG_LEVEL allows. Example: trace output needs TRON_LOG_LEVEL=trace. SPDLOG_LEVEL=trace alone leaves the sinks at debug. Only the first call of init_logging reads the variable (static flag at src/system/spdlog.cpp:36-37). No command-line flag sets the log level (no set_level call outside src/system/spdlog.cpp in src/ and h/). The pos_fake startup does not call init_logging. (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1616, h/common/assert.hpp:82-83). rederive.interactions: TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS must not be above this value. On a pool of 16 or more workers the default minimum is 1 (h/tron/models/model.hpp:75-76), so TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS=0 alone aborts there. Set TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS=0 as well. The count of one pass is min(parallelism the model plugin reports, min(max, max(min, n))) (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2413-2415). Each wait step is then a plain pause instruction (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:156-194). delay_ns then uses its time-stamp-counter spin loop for the last part of a delay (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:286-299). Intel CPU without RTM: warning 'INIT: Intel CPU without RTM (TSX): spin+pause fallback costs 13-30% decode; enable TSX ...' (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:76-77).

A test reads the same name with its own getenv (t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:239).

entries.notes: The speed estimates split attention work between the attention workers (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2433). They are not used when the model config has pay_for_determinism set. rederive.audience_reason: A constant of an internal estimator. No document, script or test in the checkout names it, and a bad value aborts the process. The inventory says operator; that is a classification choice, not a fact error.
rederive.default: Unset: 0.1 (constructor default at h/tron/threading.hpp:522).
rederive.effect: Sets how strongly each worker's speed estimate is pulled toward the mean of all workers at each update. The factor is exp(-value / timescale) (h/tron/threading.hpp:531 and :553-572). 0 removes the pull. A larger value pulls harder.
rederive.empty_value: Parses as 0.0. That value is accepted: the pull toward the group mean is then off.
rederive.how_to_check: No log line prints the value. When the pool is destroyed the info line 'Worker speeds: [...]' shows the estimates, not the setting (h/tron/threading.hpp:535). On a negative value the abort message is 'TRON_ASSERT((prior_strength) >= (0.0f)): Expected prior_strength >= 0.0f, but got <value> < 0.'
rederive.interactions: The timescale in the formula is TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE or its default 10. The speed estimates split the attention work between the attention workers (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2422-2446). With pay_for_determinism the estimates are not used (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2426-2431). The estimator is updated once for each attention plan, so once per forward pass (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2424 and :2678). No command-line flag sets it.
rederive.invalid_value: Non-numeric text parses as 0.0 and is accepted without a message. A negative value fails TRON_ASSERT_GE at h/tron/threading.hpp:529 and the process aborts when the thread pool is built. TRON_ASSERT is active in every build type (h/common/assert.hpp:3-5 and :69-75). It logs the message, logs 'Aborting.' and calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:57-63).
rederive.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH

doc_mentions.claim: Section "Selecting categories in-process". In-process captures (runtron --trace FILE, --trace-gen FILE, the SIGUSR1 tracer when TRACE_FILE names a path, and rinzler FUSE captures that set no categories) take their category selection from TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES (lines 267-272).

Design doc: the initial release of hardware KV attention requires TRON_USE_SPECULATION=0, which means EAGLE speculation is disabled.

entries.default: Off when unset. An empty value is also off.
entries.effect: When on, get_scheduler looks for a registered model named eagle-<model id> for every model it loads. If one exists, it attaches an EAGLE draft scheduler, and generation uses speculative decoding.
entries.name: TRON_USE_SPECULATION
entries.notes: Without the variable, the same lookup runs only when the model config has support_eagle set (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:59). The lookup first tries eagle-<model id>. If that is not registered, it tries the name with the parts -good, -fast, -nice and -best removed (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:37). When an eagle model is found, get_scheduler also sets support_eagle in the model config (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:60). Nothing changes when no eagle model is registered. The draft tree is tuned with TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE, TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH and TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH.

Missing: rinzler with speculation on answers HTTP 400 to logprobs (non-gemma models), structured output, tool calling and reasoning_budget_tokens (src/rinzler.cpp:3229-3305). 3. rederive.effect: When on, get_scheduler looks for a compiled-in model named eagle-<model id> for each model it loads. If that name is not registered, it removes the parts -good, -fast, -nice and -best and looks again. If a model is found, get_scheduler sets support_eagle in the model config, loads the EAGLE model with 1 layer from its default path, and attaches it as a draft scheduler (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:28-81). rinzler then generates with speculative decoding (src/rinzler.cpp:3380, src/tron/scheduler/full.cpp:357-362, src/tron/generation.cpp:51-56). If no EAGLE model is registered, nothing changes and nothing is logged.

There is no line when the variable is on and no EAGLE model is registered. In rinzler the HTTP 400 texts '... is not supported with speculation' also show that a draft is attached.
rederive.interactions: rinzler with an attached draft answers HTTP 400 to four kinds of request: logprobs (when the model slug does not start with gemma), structured output, tool calling, and reasoning_budget_tokens (src/rinzler.cpp:3229-3305). runtron: without --draft-model, runtron removes the speculator again (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:682-691), so the variable only loads and attaches the EAGLE model and runtron does not speculate. runtron --draft-model eagle sets support_eagle itself (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1475) and uses the draft (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:973-974); with that flag and no EAGLE model the process aborts with 'No EAGLE model found for <model>' (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:82-85). The variable alone never aborts. A config with support_eagle is rejected for pipeline stages: 'EAGLE speculation does not support pipeline stages' (h/tron/models/model.hpp:893-894). The value is read before main (or when the scheduler library is loaded), so it must be in the environment when the process starts. The draft tree is tuned with TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE, TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH and TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH. rinzler_proxy and rinzler_mock do not run this read: they have their own get_scheduler (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:87, src/tron/scheduler/mock.cpp:67).

entries.values: Integer parsed with atol. 0, a negative number or text that is not a number turns hardware attention off for all models. A number N above 0 turns it on for all eligible models and also sets the engagement point: N is cut to at most 2^30, rounded up to k*128 - 1 (128 is POS_PER_PAGE), and never below 127 (MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN). So 1 gives 127 and 128 gives 255 (src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:19-33, h/libpos.hpp:78, 91).

entries.default: Unset: each model uses its compiled default, and the engagement point is token position 127. The default is on when the model plugin defines force_hw_attn = true and off otherwise; the ingest code generator emits that constant (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:258). An empty value parses as 0, which is off for all models.
entries.effect: Selects whether attention runs on the FPGA cards or in software. With N > 0 it also sets the first 0-based token position of a sequence that hardware attention serves; software serves all positions below it.
entries.name: USE_HW_ATTN
entries.notes: Engagement point for N > 0: N is capped at 2^30, then pages = (N + 128) / 128 by integer division, and the point is max(127, pages * 128 - 1). So N from 1 to 127 gives 127 and N = 128 gives 255. The value is read once per process. The variable cannot force hardware attention. Each of these keeps a model in software: a pipeline stage that does not hold the embedding layer (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1791), a model shape that is not eligible or an EAGLE draft model (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1803), a hardware attention scale that the device cannot represent (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1808), no POS device (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1816), too little EMEM (the FPGA memory that holds the Q.K dot products) and an activation format that the device cannot read (h/tron/models/model.hpp:769-786). There are 14 reader lines in this area; 6 are listed. The other 8 are helper calls: hw_attn_engagement_point at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1864, :2966, :3065, :3067 and h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2110, and use_hw_attn_for_this_model at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1817, :2891 and h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2151. h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:863 (outside this area) also calls hw_attn_engagement_point().
